title.narrative: Strengthened capacity of member States to ratify and apply international labour standards and to fulfil their reporting obligations

description.narrative:
Africa has made significant progress in ratifying international labour conventions, with many ratifications in 2022-2023, thanks to targeted support from the International Labour Organization (ILO). This support focuses on regional priorities such as the African Continental Free Trade Area (ACfTA), the rule of law and the protection of vulnerable workers, including migrant and domestic workers, and victims of gender-based violence. In particular, Namibia, Mauritius, Somalia and South Africa ratified Convention No. 190 on violence and harassment at work. In addition, the ratification of Conventions Nos 97 and 143 highlights the importance of managing labour migration.
The ILO's Standards Review Mechanism is helping Africa update its commitments to modern standards, reducing outdated technical instruments and reporting obligations. Eight more ratifications are needed for full regional coverage of fundamental Conventions, notably from Liberia, Somalia, South Sudan, Morocco, Kenya and Guinea Bissau. In 2023, several African countries missed the reporting deadline, with 45% not meeting their obligations. The ILO aims to improve this through cooperation and strategic compliance planning for labour inspectorates. Building national capacity on International Labour Standards (ILS) is crucial and involves tripartite dialogue, capacity building and partnerships with non-traditional partners. The ILO's intervention is in line with its Programme and Budget 2024-25, which focuses on awareness raising, capacity building and good practices to support ratification and reporting.
